ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: new clothes
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Tattered rags, a dead raider's shirt, or nothing at all: this colonist wants something decent to wear.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: {FOR_nameDef} no longer wears tattered or dead people's clothes. Make some at a tailoring spot or bench, or buy some.

plain.li: My clothes are more holes than cloth at this point. Could someone make me something new?
I'm wearing a dead man's shirt. It still smells like him. New clothes, please.
I've let the hem out twice and patched both knees. There's nothing left to mend.
[trigger:naked] I'm not wearing enough to be decent, let alone warm. Please, anything to put on.
[winter] It's winter, and my coat lets the wind straight through.
[trait:Greedy] I deserve better than rags.
[afterraid] My shirt got torn open in the fight. I need a new one.

warm.li: When the tailor has a moment, a new shirt would be lovely. Anything that fits, really.

blunt.li: I look like a scarecrow that lost a fight. Get me some clothes.

cheerful.li: I'd love a new outfit! Something with pockets, if the tailor can manage it.

gloomy.li: Every time I get dressed I think about who wore these last, and how they died.

cold.li: Replace my clothes. I'm tired of people looking at the holes instead of at me.

plain.li: {FOR_nameDef} is walking around in rags. Could someone make {FOR_objective} something decent to wear?

warm.li: Poor {FOR_nameDef} has been wearing the same torn clothes for ages. Let's make {FOR_objective} a nice new set.

plain.li: Clean clothes that never belonged to a corpse. Thank you.
[winter] Warm clothes without a single hole in them.

cheerful.li: Look at me! Do I look dashing? I feel dashing.

plain.li: I'll patch these up one more time.
[winter] I'll shiver. I'm good at it by now.

gloomy.li: I'll wear these till they rot off me.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a proper burial for {OTHER_nameDef}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: Someone this colonist loved or respected still lies unburied, and they want the body laid to rest.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: {OTHER_nameDef}'s body rests in a grave or sarcophagus. Cremation also counts.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is still lying out there. Please, give {OTHER_objective} a proper grave.
I can't stop thinking about {OTHER_nameDef} lying out in the open. Let's bury {OTHER_objective}.
Whatever we can spare, let's spare it for {OTHER_nameDef}'s grave.
[trigger:death] We haven't even buried {OTHER_nameDef} yet. Let's do it today, before dark.
[trigger:death] I can't walk past that spot anymore. {OTHER_nameDef} deserves a grave.
[rain] It's been raining on {OTHER_nameDef} all day. Please bring {OTHER_objective} in.
[trait:Psychopath] The body is a morale problem. Bury it.
[old] I've buried a lot of people over the years. Every one of them got a grave, and this one should too.

warm.li: I'll dig the grave myself if I have to. {OTHER_nameDef} would have done it for me.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is rotting in the dirt while we go about our day. Bury {OTHER_objective}. Now.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} always made me laugh. Let's give {OTHER_objective} a good send-off.

gloomy.li: Every time I walk past, there's {OTHER_nameDef}. I can't keep seeing that.

cold.li: An unburied body brings scavengers. I'd rather not watch {OTHER_nameDef} go that way.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is at rest now. Thank you for that.
I said my goodbyes. It was done right.
Rest well, {OTHER_nameDef}. We'll take it from here.
[rain] At least the rain can't reach {OTHER_nameDef} now.

warm.li: Thank you for giving {OTHER_nameDef} the farewell {OTHER_pronoun} deserved.

gloomy.li: At least {OTHER_nameDef} doesn't have to lie out there anymore.

plain.li: So there was no time to bury {OTHER_nameDef}.
I'll never forgive this place for leaving {OTHER_nameDef} out there.

gloomy.li: We'll all end up like {OTHER_nameDef}, left in the dirt.

blunt.li: Remember this when it's your turn.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a replacement for {FOR_possessive} {SUBJECT}
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A colonist missing a body part wants it replaced, and the colony can get or make something that fits.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: {FOR_possessive} {SUBJECT} is replaced, for example with {THING}. Craft or buy one, then have a doctor install it.

plain.li: Life without my {SUBJECT} is hard. I've heard we could get {THING}.
I keep reaching for things with a {SUBJECT} I don't have. Could the doctor fit me with {THING}?
[trigger:injury] I keep forgetting it's gone. Then I try to use it.
I want to be useful again, or as close to it as I can get.
[old] I've got years of work left in me if someone fixes me up.

warm.li: I don't want to be a burden. With {THING}, I could pull my weight again.

blunt.li: I'm missing my {SUBJECT}. Fix it. You know how.

cheerful.li: I've decided I want {THING}. I'm already practicing showing it off.

gloomy.li: Every day I'm reminded of what I lost. Maybe {THING} would make it stop.

cold.li: Without my {SUBJECT}, I do the work of half a person. Replace it and you'll have a whole one again.

plain.li: {FOR_nameDef} has been struggling without {FOR_possessive} {SUBJECT}. Could we get {FOR_objective} {THING}?
It's not what I was born with, but it works. Thank you.
I'll learn it. Give me a week and you won't know it isn't mine.

cheerful.li: Look at this! I can't stop testing it.

gloomy.li: It's not the same, but it's close enough to be going on with.

cold.li: It works. Tell the doctor I've no complaints.

plain.li: I'll keep working around it, the way I have been.
I'll manage. I've managed so far.

gloomy.li: I'll be like this for good, then.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: an animal companion
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: An animal lover has spotted a creature out on the map and wants to bring it home.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.lostText: {OTHER_nameDef}, the companion {FOR_nameDef} wanted, is no longer the colony's.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: The colony tames a new animal. There's a {SUBJECT} out there, for a start.

plain.li: There's a {SUBJECT} wandering around out there. I think it wants to come home with us.
Could I try taming that {SUBJECT}? I'd look after it, I swear.
[winter] A warm animal to curl up next to would get me through this winter.
[lowmood] I'd like an animal to look after. It would give me a reason to get up in the morning.
[child] Can we have a pet? I'll feed it every day, I promise.

warm.li: That {SUBJECT} looks lonely. We could use a friend, and so could it.

blunt.li: There's a perfectly good {SUBJECT} out there doing nothing. Let me tame it.

cheerful.li: I saw a {SUBJECT} out past the fields! I've already picked a name for it.

gloomy.li: I get on better with animals than with people. Let me tame that {SUBJECT}.

cold.li: I've watched that {SUBJECT} for three days. It comes to the same spot at dusk. It'll come to me.

plain.li: Welcome to the family, little one.
Look at its face. I'm going to spoil it rotten.

cheerful.li: Come and say hello to our new friend!

gloomy.li: Finally, someone around here who's glad to see me.

plain.li: It wandered off. I watched it go.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: stronger defenses
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A fighter, or someone shaken by violence, doesn't feel safe and wants better defenses. What they ask for depends on what the colony can build.

plain.li: Next raid, I'd like more than a doorframe to hide behind. Let's add more {SUBJECT}.
Our defenses are thin. A few more {SUBJECT} would let me sleep at night.
I've been walking the perimeter. We need {SUBJECT} at the approaches.
[trigger:raid] They walked right up to our door. Next time I want something between them and us.
[trigger:raid] We were lucky today. I don't want to count on that next time.
[trigger:raid,lowtech] Spikes in the ground and a wall to hide behind. That's all I ask.
[hurt] I've got the stitches to prove we need better defenses.
[night] I keep hearing things at night. I'd sleep better knowing we're ready.

warm.li: I count heads after every raid. I'd like to stop counting. More {SUBJECT}, please.

blunt.li: We're sitting ducks. Build more {SUBJECT} before they come back.

cheerful.li: Let's make the next raiders regret coming! I'm thinking {SUBJECT}, and plenty of them.

gloomy.li: They'll come again, and we're not ready for them.

cold.li: I've walked the approaches the way a raider would. I know where I'd come in. Put more {SUBJECT} there.

plain.li: That's better. Now they'll have to work for it.
[night] Let them come. We're ready now.

cheerful.li: Ha! I almost feel sorry for the next raiders.

gloomy.li: Safer than we were, at least.

cold.li: They'll lose more people getting in now.

plain.li: I'll sleep with my weapon by the bed.
[afterraid] We'll do it the hard way, then. With blood.

gloomy.li: When they come, remember I asked.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a {SUBJECT} worthy of {FOR_possessive} title
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A noble's title comes with expectations for their bedroom or throne room, and they're not being met.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: Every {SUBJECT} requirement of {FOR_possessive} title is met.

plain.li: My title carries certain expectations. My {SUBJECT} does not yet meet them.
I'm sure you understand that someone of my rank cannot be seen living like this.

warm.li: I don't ask for myself, truly. But my title must be honored, for all our sakes.

blunt.li: A noble in a hovel. It's embarrassing for all of us. Fix my {SUBJECT}.

cheerful.li: Oh, I have such plans for my {SUBJECT}! Gold, marble, maybe a harp.

gloomy.li: If the Empire saw how I live, they'd strip my title on the spot.

cold.li: My {SUBJECT} is below the required standard. Correct it.

plain.li: At last, rooms befitting my station.

cheerful.li: It's magnificent! I feel positively regal.

cold.li: This meets the standard. You may go.

plain.li: I shall endure this indignity. I shall also remember it.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: {THING} to learn and play at
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A child wants somewhere of their own to learn and play.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.lostText: The {THINGBARE} {FOR_nameDef} learned and played at is gone.

plain.li: Can we have {THING}? Please? I'll be good.
All the grown-ups have stuff to do. I want stuff too, like {THING}!
[child] There's nothing to do here! Not for kids, anyway.
[winter,child] It's too cold to play outside. Can we have something inside?

cheerful.li: If we get {THING}, I'll learn everything, even the boring stuff!

gloomy.li: There's nothing for kids here. Just work and raiders.

plain.li: It's mine? Really mine? Best day ever!
I'm going to use it every day, even when I don't have to!
Grown-ups never listen.
I asked and asked, and nothing happened.
